content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles and underperform in late cycles.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with price corrections, especially when sentiment peaks after a forecast peak.", "Model bias toward higher prices persists despite historical mean-reversion signals.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with recent price trends rather than isolated spikes.", "Lagging sentiment indicators often precede price reversals, suggesting predictive value beyond immediate forecasts.", "Models exhibit diminishing accuracy as price volatility increases, particularly after sentiment shifts to negative.", "Forecast overshoots are more common in bullish sentiment cycles, followed by sharp corrections.", "Sentiment-driven corrections often outpace model predictions, indicating sentiment has stronger predictive power in downturns."]}
